answer: Adaptive arrival spacing requires each identity’s first transactions to arrive with inter-arrival gaps drawn from a heavy-tailed schedule; a violet rate-limiter flags bursts that cluster tighter than the learned median gap. When traffic from one source exceeds that envelope, admission slows to a copper-throttled queue that only clears as the source sustains spacing over hours. Genuine users pay nothing beyond a little nectar of patience, while each added fake identity must rent distinct egress and hold it open long enough to clear the queue.
